# Two node props that read each other have no answer.
#
# A prop read off a `#id` whose node the target keeps nothing of is answered
# with the expression the prop was given, and answering runs to a fixed point
# because one answer can uncover the next -- `circle #b(r=a.r)` is a read that
# only becomes readable once `a`'s own props are known.
#
# A cycle has no fixed point to reach. It is detected before any substitution
# rather than discovered by running out of stack, which is what a depth guard
# would have done: the graph is known, so the question can be asked outright.
#
# The same shape one layer down -- a window prop that reads itself -- is only
# guarded in consteval today, and is the reason PLAN.md says a checker rule
# about self-reference is the real answer to both.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out .
stderr 'reads its own value back'
stderr 'nothing to answer with'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import draw "sngl:ui/draw"

ui.window #w(title="t") {
    draw.canvas(width=10px, height=10px) {
        draw.circle #a(cx=1.0, cy=1.0, r=b.r)
        draw.circle #b(cx=2.0, cy=2.0, r=a.r)
    }

    ui.text(value="a is {a.r}")
}
